parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
ken is one's range of knowledge or sight, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A military force has seized a stretch of ground or a firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a firing range in the army picture, but here it means scope of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seized or caught has been taken, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Whereby pilot checks river running here

parts.note: the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, England
running away is flight, as in 'put to flight'

explanation.surface: An airman inspects a river with water rushing past.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a Hampshire chalk stream well known to anglers; 'here' just closes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run in the air is how an aviator verifies that a plane performs properly.

indicators.note: with no English means the abbreviation for English is dropped from the word for cattle

parts.note: kine is an old plural meaning cows or cattle

explanation.surface: Livestock of no English breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood in the sense of family or lineage, as in 'blood is thicker than water', means relatives.

clue.text: It protects consumer when the chips are down

definitions.text: It protects consumer when the chips are down

parts.words: It protects consumer when the chips are down
parts.note: read literally: a diner (consumer) is shielded when fried chips fall into the lap, not in a crisis

explanation.surface: Something that safeguards shoppers in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When the chips are down' is an idiom for a crisis and 'consumer' suggests consumer protection; really it is someone eating, and chips dropping on their lap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth spread on the lap at table catches dropped food such as chips.

parts.note: ARA, Associate of the Royal Academy, is a crossword stand-in for an artist
a capital letter is upper case, abbreviated to UC
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A painter has shortened the title of a song about a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city, but it is a capital letter; 'abbreviated' shortens upper case to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey-puzzle tree is a conifer that keeps its leaves all year round.

parts.note: read literally: a car that can travel over the seas, driving straight into water

explanation.surface: A car meant to be driven abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseas' suggests abroad; it means literally over the sea, a vehicle at home on land and water.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that travels both on land and in water is named after creatures like frogs that live in both.

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England
'dee' is how the letter D is said, so it stands for that letter

explanation.surface: A Welsh-English river has been given publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a real river, so the solver looks for a river synonym; instead it is the spoken name of the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Views that were broadcast or made known have been aired.

clue.text: Poetry lover's work that is without appeal at first

indicators.note: at first places the word for appeal at the front of the answer

parts.note: to call is to appeal or make a request

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the abbreviation for that is goes round the work

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A verse enthusiast's output, which has nothing attractive to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense, outside; 'at first' puts the appeal at the front. The 's after 'lover' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse of epic verse in Greek myth is the patron and devotee of the art.

clue.text: Slowing down, learn to land in formation

indicators.note: in formation suggests aircraft, but signals that the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A trainee pilot is told to ease off and touch down with the squadron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in formation' rearranges LEARN TO LAND; the answer is a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term tells players to gradually reduce tempo.

definitions.meaning: the curved underside of the foot between heel and toes
a curved span over an opening, as in a bridge or doorway

explanation.definitionFit: The raised curve of the sole and a curved span are both called by the same word.

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth or polish it
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: A newspaper from Poland can be harsh in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to suggest Poland, but it is the verb, to polish: SAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit-coated paper is a common abrasive for smoothing surfaces.

indicators.note: turning means those leading letters are churned into a different order
leading characters in keeps only the front of the answer to 6 down, dropping its tail

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, the Muse of epic poetry

explanation.surface: The first letters of a clue are changing colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the leading characters of 6 down drops its last three letters, leaving CALLI, which 'turning' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: Stronghold provided that is protecting old king's port, perhaps

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold
if means provided that

indicators.note: protecting means the abbreviation for that is surrounds the king's name, shielding it

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is
Edwin was a seventh-century king of Northumbria

explanation.surface: A fortress keeps watch over an ancient monarch's harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests a harbour in the military picture, but it is the drink; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a wine strengthened with added brandy, one example of the type.

indicators.note: orders, read as a verb, means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A naval commander sounds the alert against an attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' looks like the officer commanding, but it is the anagram signal on RAIDER ALARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval rank just below vice admiral is a senior commissioned officer.

parts.note: the post held by the person who has the last word on what gets printed in a newspaper

explanation.surface: The duty of whoever has the last say.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a publication decides finally what appears, and that role is the office in question.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to run goods is to smuggle them; ran is the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone was brought illegally across a border.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'run' guns or drugs is to smuggle them, so 'smuggled' gives RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly Persia.

definitions.meaning: wasteful and given to indulgence, a dissolute way of living
used up or squandered, as of a fortune that has run out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both living a debauched life and having been frittered away entirely.

parts.note: an unmarried woman is jokingly said to be 'on the shelf', so her lifetime is spent there

explanation.surface: How long an unmarried woman lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' is an old idiom for a woman thought past marrying; the phrase really means how long goods last in store.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the time a product stays fit to sell, punning on a spinster's time 'on the shelf'.

parts.note: an airing is an outing in the fresh air

explanation.surface: Leading a parish outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To head a meeting as its president is to chair it.

clue.text: Polls may move to his advantage

definitions.text: Polls may move to his advantage

parts.words: Polls may move to his advantage
parts.note: read with polls as heads: a recruiter gains when people (heads) switch jobs, not election polls shifting

explanation.surface: A politician benefits from shifting opinion polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polls' suggests elections; it is an old word for heads, here people moving between employers.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruitment agent who poaches staff profits when executives change jobs.

definitions.meaning: to furrow, as when brows are drawn together in a frown
to join or unite closely, as broken bones mend together

explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to furrow the brow and to bind together firmly.

parts.note: from the British saying 'Bob's your uncle', meaning there you are
a tom is a male cat; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A relative named Tom owns a creature from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle Tom' suggests the novel; split it as 'Your Uncle' (Bob, from 'Bob's your uncle') and 'Tom' (a male cat).
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx-like wild feline of North America with a short tail.

clue.text: Married helpers of queen, perhaps? On the contrary

definitions.text: Married helpers of queen, perhaps? On the contrary

parts.words: Married helpers of queen, perhaps? On the contrary
parts.note: reversing the sense gives unmarried attendants of a queen, or of a bride

explanation.surface: Wedded assistants to a monarch, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'Married' to unmarried: the attendants are maidens, not wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwed women attending a queen or bride bear this title.

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the farewell phrase is lopped off

parts.note: so long is an informal way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: A wise elder's goodbye was abruptly ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'sage' reads as 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Solon was an Athenian lawgiver, one of the Seven Wise Men of Greece, so a wise man.

clue.text: Farm with well-established lines of chestnuts, perhaps

definitions.text: Farm with well-established lines of chestnuts, perhaps

parts.words: Farm with well-established lines of chestnuts, perhaps
parts.note: chestnuts as horses of that colour, bred on a farm in established bloodlines, not trees in rows

explanation.surface: An orchard with old rows of chestnut trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnuts' and 'lines' suggest planted trees; they are chestnut horses and pedigree lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding establishment for horses keeps animals of proven pedigree.

parts.note: tars, short for tarpaulins, is slang for sailors

explanation.surface: Skeletons recovered from an island belonging to seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsal bones form the ankle region, and the plural of tarsus names them.

clue.text: Left new order for thin, cool garment

indicators.note: new order for means the letters of the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone departed with fresh instructions for light, airy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thin, cool' reads as a description of the garment, but it is the material that 'new order for' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth worn wrapped round the hips is a simple item of dress.

clue.text: Fuel millions can be seen to be using up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

indicators.text: can be seen to be using
indicators.note: can be seen means the letters sit visibly inside the word millions

explanation.surface: Energy that millions are evidently burning through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be seen' hides LIO inside 'millions'; 'up' turns it round, reading upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is burned as a source of energy.

definitions.meaning: steady effort and industriousness, as in applying oneself
a public stagecoach formerly used in France

explanation.definitionFit: The word means persistent careful effort and also an old horse-drawn passenger vehicle in France.

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals that the letters of lit up are jumbled into a surprise order

explanation.surface: A light bulb suddenly came on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' and 'lit up' suggest a light bulb; it is a flower bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring flowers of this kind grow from an underground storage organ.
